findings.source_quote: ἐπὶ πλεῖον αὐτοὺς πεπλανημένους ἐλέγξαι θέλων
findings.english_quote: wishing to expose them as having gone still further astray
findings.issue: The main rendering defensibly attaches ἐπὶ πλεῖον to their being astray, but the phrase can instead qualify ἐλέγξαι: wishing to demonstrate their error more fully. These readings distinguish greater error from a fuller demonstration of error. The existing note discusses the attachment of τοὺς προφήτας but does not disclose this separate scope ambiguity. This is an interpretive disclosure issue, not evidence of source corruption.
findings.suggested_revision: Extend the note to preserve both scopes. For example: “The main rendering takes ἐπὶ πλεῖον with the following αὐτοὺς πεπλανημένους, expressing a greater degree of error. Alternatively, it can qualify ἐλέγξαι: ‘wishing to demonstrate more fully that they had gone astray.’ The position before the predicative phrase supports the chosen attachment, but does not exclude the alternative.” The main wording may remain as a disclosed contextual choice; the revised note requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: καθ’ ὃν λόγον Μωϋσῆς ἑπτὰ συνεχώρησεν γαμεῖν
findings.english_quote: on what grounds Moses had allowed seven to marry
findings.issue: The draft defensibly treats ἑπτά as the subject of γαμεῖν, but the indeclinable numeral can also be its object: permission to marry seven. That alternative materially changes the marriage question. The note's statement that no object of “marry” is supplied describes the chosen analysis, not an unambiguous property of the Greek, and the alternative is not preserved.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the current main rendering only with an expanded note identifying the subject/object ambiguity: “ἑπτά is taken here as the infinitive's subject, ‘allowed seven [people] to marry,’ a contextual reading of the Sadducees' question. It could instead be the object, ‘allowed [someone] to marry seven [people].’ The wording does not explicitly identify the seven as brothers, men, or women. Under the chosen subject reading, the object of ‘marry’ remains unstated.” Do not import a spouse or other narrative details into the main text. The revised disclosure requires fresh review; no print verification or emendation is needed for this ambiguity.
